# The flows that rivus finds in its own code as it is on macOS (TestDogfood, the darwin view: GOOS=darwin, read statically on any system). Same
# format and rules as dogfood-flows.txt (the Linux view); this view also reads the code that is only for macOS: the sandbox (internal/sandbox) and the
# call of it that runs the programs of a Rust project (cmd/rivus/isolate_sandbox_darwin.go). What the flags name (the project, the
# extractor, a path to read) reaches the programs that the sandbox runs and the files it prepares: that is what a CLI that runs a
# build under a sandbox does, and it is what the analysis must find in its own code.

cmd/rivus.runAnalyze -> (*cmd/rivus.analyzeOpts).analyze [os.Create]  # the same kind of flow as in the Linux view: what a flag names reaches a file or a program of the command that uses it
cmd/rivus.runAnalyze -> (*cmd/rivus.analyzeOpts).analyze [os.Create]  # the same kind of flow as in the Linux view: what a flag names reaches a file or a program of the command that uses it

cmd/rivus.runAnalyze -> cmd/rivus.readIR [os.Open]  # the same kind of flow as in the Linux view: what a flag names reaches a file or a program of the command that uses it
cmd/rivus.runAnalyze -> cmd/rivus.writeFuncValues [os.Create]  # the path of -func-values (an output file of analyze: the table of the diagnostic); the other commands share the flags
